lines.trans: I am not ready to take such a sin upon my soul.
I could not allow you to take such a risk.
Nothing would have happened to me!
First your tongue would have gone completely numb.
Elya, I thought for a long time and wanted to say...
Then you would have been thrown into a sudden fever.
And severe itching would have started right away.
Dima, tell me, are you alright right now?
Then your coordination and speech would have failed.
I have made an important manly decision...
Elya, please marry me!

examples.text: Я выхожу через минуту.
examples.trans: I'm going out in a minute.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').

examples.text: Эля, выходи, пожалуйста, за меня замуж!
examples.trans: Elya, please marry me!

examples.text: Нет, Катя, выслушай меня, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: No, Katya, hear me out, please.

examples.text: Кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: A coffee, please.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Буквально минуту назад она мне улыбалась.
examples.trans: Literally a minute ago she was smiling at me.

examples.text: Ничего особенного, она просто засыпает.
examples.trans: Nothing special, she is simply falling asleep.

examples.text: Тогда быстро за работу, бездельники!
examples.trans: Then get back to work quickly, slackers!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'married (of a woman)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я незаметно заменил твой кусок филе на свой.
examples.trans: I quietly replaced your piece of fillet with mine.

examples.text: Я заменил твой кусок филе.
examples.trans: I swapped your piece of fillet.

examples.text: Эля, выходи, пожалуйста, за меня замуж!
examples.trans: Elya, please marry me!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А вы думали, что от меня избавились?
examples.trans: And did you think that you had gotten rid of me?

examples.text: Что, шеф, на большие деньги повелись?
examples.trans: Well, Chef, did you fall for the big money?

examples.text: Прости, что я тебе тогда не сказала.
examples.trans: Forgive me for not telling you back then.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'чему').

examples.text: Огузок, почему ты снова опаздываешь на смену?
examples.trans: Oguzok, why are you late for your shift again?

examples.text: Вот почему у тебя такие сильные, красивые руки.
examples.trans: That is why you have such strong, handsome hands.

examples.text: Дима, что с тобой, почему ты молчишь?
examples.trans: Dima, what is wrong with you, why are you silent?

meanings.en: to be silent, to keep quiet
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'are silent', paired with 'замолчать'.

examples.text: Почему ты молчишь?
examples.trans: Why aren't you saying anything?

examples.text: Ну что ты молчишь? Ты толстый, ты не спортсмен!
examples.trans: Well, why are you so quiet? You're fat, you're no athlete!

examples.text: Молчи и просто работай.
examples.trans: Stay silent and just work.
